questions.stem:
The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as:
$\Delta H$ | $\Delta S$ | Temperature | Spontaneity
(A) | $+$ | $-$ | any $T$ | Non spontaneous
(B) | $+$ | $+$ | low $T$ | spontaneous
(C) | $-$ | $-$ | low $T$ | Non spontaneous
(D) | $-$ | $+$ | any $T$ | spontaneous
questions.solution:
$\because\ \Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$
For spontaneity of reaction : $\Delta G = -\text{ve}$

questions.stem:
Standard electrode potentials for a few half cells are mentioned below:
$E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}} = 0.34\,\mathrm{V},\ E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0.76\,\mathrm{V}$
$E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ag^{+}/Ag}} = 0.80\,\mathrm{V},\ E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Mg^{2+}/Mg}} = -2.37\,\mathrm{V}$
Which one of the following cells gives the most negative value of $\Delta G^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution:
$\because\ \Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}$
Option (1) $E^{\circ} = 0.8 + 0.76 = 1.56\ \mathrm{V}$
$\therefore\ \Delta G^{\circ} = -2 \times F \times 1.56 = -3.12\ \mathrm{V}$
Option (2) $E^{\circ} = -2.37 + 0.76 = -1.61\ \mathrm{V}$
$\therefore\ \Delta G^{\circ} = -2 \times F \times (-1.61) = +3.22\ \mathrm{V}$
Option (3) $E^{\circ} = -2.37 - 0.8 = -3.17\ \mathrm{V}$
$\therefore\ \Delta G^{\circ} = -2 \times F \times (-3.17) = +6.34$
Option (4) $E^{\circ} = 0.8 - 0.34 = 0.46\ \mathrm{V}$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2 \times F \times 0.46 = -0.92\ \mathrm{V}$

questions.stem:
Consider the reaction
$\mathrm{X_2Y(g) \rightleftharpoons X_2(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}Y_2(g)}$
The equation representing correct relationship between the degree of dissociation (x) of $\mathrm{X_2Y(g)}$ with its equilibrium constant $K_p$ is________. Assume x to be very very small.
questions.solution:
1 mole
$\mathrm{X_2Y_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons X_{2(g)} + \tfrac{1}{2}Y_{2(g)}}$
$1-x$ mole, $x$ mole, $\dfrac{x}{2}$ mole
$\therefore\ P_{\mathrm{X_2Y}} = \dfrac{1-x}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$P_{\mathrm{X_2}} = \dfrac{x}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$P_{\mathrm{Y_2}} = \dfrac{x/2}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P$
$\therefore\ K_p = \left(\dfrac{x}{1+\frac{x}{2}}P\right)\left(\dfrac{x}{2\left(1+\frac{x}{2}\right)}P\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Big/ \left(\dfrac{1-x}{1+\frac{x}{2}} \times P\right)$
$\therefore\ K_p = \left(\dfrac{x}{1-x}\right)\left(\dfrac{x}{2\left(1+\frac{x}{2}\right)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \times p^{\frac{1}{2}}$
$\because$ x to be very very small
$\therefore\ K_p = \dfrac{x^{3/2}}{(2)^{\frac{1}{2}}} \times P^{\frac{1}{2}}$
$\therefore\ x^{\frac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{K_p \times 2^{\frac{1}{2}}}{P^{\frac{1}{2}}}$
$\therefore\ x^{3} = \dfrac{K_p^{2} \times 2}{P}$
$x = \left(\dfrac{K_p^{2} \times 2}{P}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$

questions.stem: When a non-volatile solute is added to the solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreases by 10 mm of Hg. The mole fraction of the solute in the solution is 0.2. What would be the mole fraction of the solvent if decrease in vapour pressure is 20 mm of Hg ?
questions.solution:
$\because\ P^{\circ} - P \propto X_{\mathrm{solute}}$
and $\because\ 10 \propto 0.2$
$\therefore\ 20 \propto 0.4$
$\therefore\ X_{\mathrm{solvent}} = 1 - X_{\mathrm{solute}} = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

questions.stem: Consider a binary solution of two volatile liquid components 1 and 2. $x_1$ and $y_1$ are the mole fractions of component 1 in liquid and vapour phase, respectively. The slope and intercept of the linear plot of $\dfrac{1}{x_1}$ vs $\dfrac{1}{y_1}$ are given respectively as :
questions.solution:
$\because$ For liquid solution of two liquids '1' and '2'
$P_1 = P_T y_1 = P_1^{o} x_1$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{P_T}{x_1} = \dfrac{P_1^{o}}{y_1}$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{P_2^{o} + x_1(P_1^{o} - P_2^{o})}{x_1} = \dfrac{P_1^{o}}{y_1}$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{P_2^{o}}{x_1} + (P_1^{o} - P_2^{o}) = \dfrac{P_1^{o}}{y_1}$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{1}{x_1} = \left(\dfrac{P_1^{o}}{P_2^{o}}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{y_1}\right) + \left(\dfrac{P_2^{o} - P_1^{o}}{P_2^{o}}\right)$
$\therefore$ Slope $= \left(\dfrac{P_1^{o}}{P_2^{o}}\right)$
$\therefore$ Intercept $= \left(\dfrac{P_2^{o} - P_1^{o}}{P_2^{o}}\right)$

questions.stem: 0.01 mole of an organic compound (X) containing 10% hydrogen, on complete combustion produced 0.9 g $\mathrm{H_2O}$. Molar mass of (X) is ______ $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.solution:
Organic compound $\xrightarrow{\text{combustion}}$ $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (0.9 gm)
$\therefore$ mole of $\mathrm{H_2O} = \dfrac{0.9}{18} = 0.05$ mole
$\therefore$ mole of H in $\mathrm{H_2O} = 0.05 \times 2 = 0.1$ mole = mole of H in 0.01 mole Organic compound
$\therefore$ wt of H atom in 0.01 mole compound $= 0.1 \times 1 = 0.1$ gm
$\therefore$ wt of H atom in one mole compound $= \dfrac{0.1}{0.01} = 10$ gm
$\because$ wt. % of H $= \dfrac{\text{wt. of H in one mole compound}}{\text{Molar mass of compound}} \times 100$
$10 = \dfrac{10}{M} \times 100$
$\therefore\ M = 100$

Consider the following sequence of reactions.
Total number of $sp^{3}$ hybridised carbon atoms in the major product C formed is ________.

When 81.0 g of aluminium is allowed to react with 128.0 g of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced in grams is ____. (Nearest integer)
Given :
Molar mass of Al is $27.0\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$
Molar mass of O is $16.0\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{4Al + 3O_2 \longrightarrow 2Al_2O_3}$
$\dfrac{81}{27} = 3$ mole, $\dfrac{128}{32} = 4$ mole
Limiting reagent
$\therefore$ mole of $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ formed $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3$ mole
$\therefore$ wt. $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ formed $= \dfrac{3}{2} \times 102 = 153$ gm

questions.stem:
The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X_2}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{bond}$ calculated from the given data is _______ $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
$\mathrm{M^{+}X^{-}(s) \rightarrow M^{+}(g) + X^{-}(g)}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{lattice} = 800\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\mathrm{M(s) \rightarrow M(g)}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{sub} = 100\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\mathrm{M(g) \rightarrow M^{+}(g) + e^{-}(g)}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{i} = 500\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\mathrm{X(g) + e^{-}(g) \rightarrow X^{-}(g)}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{eg} = -300\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\mathrm{M(s) + \tfrac{1}{2}X_2(g) \rightarrow M^{+}X^{-}(s)}$ $\Delta H^{\circ}_{f} = -400\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
[Given : $\mathrm{M^{+}X^{-}}$ is a pure ionic compound and X forms a diatomic molecule $\mathrm{X_2}$ is gaseous state]
questions.solution:
$\therefore\ \Delta H_f(\mathrm{MX}) = \Delta H_{sub}(\mathrm{M}) + \mathrm{I.E.(M)} + \dfrac{1}{2}[\mathrm{B.E.(X-X)}] + \mathrm{EG(X)} + \mathrm{L.E.(MX)}$
$-400 = (100) + (500) + \dfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{B.E.}) + (-300) + (-800)$
$\therefore\ \mathrm{B.E.} = 200\ \mathrm{kJ\ mole^{-1}}$
